newsitem.title: ESTONIA: EESTI KINDLUSTUS AIMS FOR NOVEMBER LISTING.
newsitem.headline: EESTI KINDLUSTUS AIMS FOR NOVEMBER LISTING.

text.p: Eesti Kindlustus, a subsidiary of Hoiupank, said on Monday it wants to get listed on the Tallinn stock exchange by November.

The Eesti Kindlustus board is to propose to a shareholder meeting, due in the middle of May, to issue new shares via a public offer or offer existing shares via a tender, Ivar Virkus, company chairman, told Reuters.
The company, the largest insurance firm in Estonia, also plans to a representative office in St. Petersburg this year.
"We need to become acquainted with Russian legislation and the present situation to find out about a possible launch of insurance activities," Virkus added.
To get a bourse listing, the insurance company needs to have at least 25 percent of its shares must be in public issue.
"The shares will be listed by November," Virkus said.
Virkus said it was not clear how many shares it would issue. If shareholders decide to sell existing shares, the board proposal is that Hoiupank sell some of its stake, he added.
The board will also propose that shareholders retain its 1996 profit of 26 million kroons, Virkus said.
Hoiupank owns 86 percent of Eesti Kindlustus. The rest is divided between Hansa Investments, a subsidiary of Hansapank, Finnish Profit OY and Pindi Vaartpaberid, an Estonian securities company.
"In Russia, Eesti Kindlustus will most probably start in life-insurance," Virkus said.
"The insurance market is relatively sleepy there...but with huge potential," he added.
Virkus said the company is also eyeing Lithuania and Latvia but they are lower priorities.
"We will go on a fact-finding trip at the beginning of May to Lithuania," he added.
Eesti Kindlustus has a market share of 23.6 percent. It collected 188 million kroons in premiums in 1996. The company is active in life-insurance and non-life insurance.
